rics.meaning: Exports of Goods and Services (Constant) — real exports level for GDP-arithmetic. Companion to aIDCEXND/CA.
rics.how_to_use: Use for export-volume tracking. Real exports growth is the meaningful trade-cycle signal.

rics.meaning: Exports — alternate framing of merchandise exports level. Cross-check against aIDCEXPB/A.
rics.how_to_use: Use either series for tracking; minor methodological/timing differences. The standardized version (aIDCEXPB/A) aligns with OECD frameworks.

rics.meaning: Exports Growth (Actual) — Reuters poll-anchored YoY export-growth release. Markets use as benchmark forecast anchor.
rics.how_to_use: Comparison against poll consensus drives IDR same-day. Indonesia export YoY swings 30+ pp through commodity cycles.

rics.meaning: Crude Petroleum Exports — Indonesia's crude oil exports. Indonesia is a net oil importer overall but exports some crude grades (mainly to Asian refiners).
rics.how_to_use: Small share of total exports (~1-2%). Has been declining structurally as domestic demand outpaces production. Indonesia left OPEC in 2008 and again in 2016 to align with importer status. Track Brent/WTI for unit-price impact.

rics.meaning: Gas Exports — LNG plus pipeline gas exports. Indonesia is a major LNG exporter (Bontang, Tangguh terminals); main customers Japan, South Korea, China.
rics.how_to_use: Highly correlated with Asian LNG spot prices (JKM benchmark). Long-term contracts dominate volume; spot prices drive quarterly revenue swings. Tangguh expansion (Train 3) boosted capacity in 2023.

rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil and Gas — total non-O&G goods exports. ~90% of Indonesia's total goods exports.
rics.how_to_use: Strip-out oil/gas removes commodity-price-driven swings, isolating manufactures + agri + minerals (coal, palm oil, nickel). Better cyclical signal than total exports.

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, China
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, China — exports to China. Indonesia's largest single export market (~25% of non-O&G exports).
rics.how_to_use: Watch Chinese steel and EV production for leading signal. Coal + nickel + palm oil dominate. Falls sharply during China property-sector downturns (2022-23).

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Germany
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Germany — exports to Germany. ~2% of non-O&G exports. Largest items: palm oil derivatives, footwear, textiles, machinery.
rics.how_to_use: Track for European demand cycle. EU palm-oil import restrictions (deforestation regulations) affect this flow.

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Japan
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Japan — exports to Japan. ~7-8% of non-O&G exports. Largest items: coal, copper concentrates, palm oil.
rics.how_to_use: Stable bilateral. Track JKM LNG prices for related gas-export effects (Japan is Indonesia's largest LNG buyer).

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Malaysia
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Malaysia — exports to Malaysia. ~5% of non-O&G exports. Heavy in CPO crude palm oil and intermediates.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia + Malaysia are world's two largest palm oil producers. Bilateral trade reflects cross-border processing chains.

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, Singapore
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, Singapore — exports to Singapore. ~7% of non-O&G exports. Significant trans-shipment hub effect.
rics.how_to_use: Singapore is largely a trans-shipment hub — a lot of Indonesia exports to Singapore are re-exported. Track for ASEAN trade flows.

rics.description: Exports, Non oil and gas, United States of America
rics.meaning: Exports, Non-Oil/Gas, USA — exports to United States. ~10-12% of Indonesia's non-O&G exports.
rics.how_to_use: Heavy in textiles, apparel, footwear, electronics, palm oil. Track US-China trade tensions for trade-diversion benefits to Indonesia.

rics.meaning: Exports, Oil and Gas — Indonesia's oil + LNG exports. ~10% of total exports despite Indonesia being a net oil importer (gas exports offset oil imports).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks Brent/JKM (Asian LNG) prices closely. Pertamina dominates oil exports; multiple operators in LNG (Bontang, Tangguh).

rics.meaning: Petroleum Product Exports — refined petroleum products (gasoline, diesel, fuel oil). Smaller than crude exports.
rics.how_to_use: Niche. Pertamina (state oil company) exports surplus refined products from its refineries. Tracks regional refining margins.

rics.meaning: FDI YoY change — pace of FDI inflow growth. Reuters-poll-anchored release.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks BKPM realization data. Slowdowns flag investor-confidence loss.

rics.meaning: Imports of Goods and Services (Constant) — real imports level for GDP accounting.
rics.how_to_use: Use for import-volume tracking. Pairs with real exports (aIDEXNGSR/C) for net-export contribution to GDP.

rics.meaning: Imports — total merchandise imports level. Companion to aIDCIMPB/A.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. Trade aggregates may differ slightly between BPS and BoP releases due to timing.

rics.meaning: Imports Growth (Actual) — Reuters poll-anchored YoY import-growth release.
rics.how_to_use: Surprise vs consensus drives IDR. Sustained import-growth above export-growth signals widening trade deficit.

rics.meaning: Imports of Capital Goods — machinery, equipment, transport equipment. ~25% of total imports.
rics.how_to_use: Leads investment (GFCF) by 1-2 quarters. Sustained surge signals upcoming capex acceleration. Falls during BI hike cycles.

rics.meaning: Imports of Consumer Goods — finished consumer goods. Smallest share (~5%) reflecting domestic-manufacturing substitution policies.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks middle-class import-luxury demand. Sensitive to IDR (expensive imports curtailed when IDR weakens).

rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil and Gas — total non-O&G imports. ~85% of total imports.
rics.how_to_use: Strip out oil/gas for a cleaner manufacturing-input demand signal. Tracks domestic manufacturing PMI.

rics.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, China
rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, China — imports from China. Indonesia's largest single import source (~30% of non-O&G imports).
rics.how_to_use: Heavy in machinery, electronics, base metals, chemicals. Tracks China's manufacturing capacity utilization. Indonesia runs persistent bilateral deficit with China.

rics.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Germany
rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Germany — imports from Germany. ~3% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in machinery, automotive equipment, chemicals.
rics.how_to_use: Track for German auto-export and machinery cycle. EU-Indonesia trade tensions (palm oil restrictions, deforestation regulation) affect bilateral dynamics.

rics.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Japan
rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Japan — imports from Japan. ~10% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in machinery, transport equipment, electronics.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks Japanese auto + industrial-machinery exports. Stable bilateral.

rics.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, Malaysia
rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, Malaysia — imports from Malaysia. ~5% of non-O&G imports. ASEAN trade flows; petrochemicals, intermediates.
rics.how_to_use: Track ASEAN regional supply-chain dynamics. Tariff harmonization under AEC supports this flow.

rics.description: Imports, Non oil and gas, USA
rics.meaning: Imports, Non-Oil/Gas, USA — imports from USA. ~5% of non-O&G imports. Heavy in capital goods, agricultural products (soybeans, cotton).
rics.how_to_use: Track for US-Indonesia trade flows. Trump-era trade tensions (2018-2020, again 2025+) affect tariff-sensitive items.

rics.meaning: Imports, Oil and Gas — Indonesia's oil products + LPG imports. ~15% of total imports. Indonesia is a net oil importer (refining capacity short of consumption).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks Brent prices + IDR (cost-pass-through). Surges drive trade deficit and energy-subsidy bill. Major government-finance variable.

rics.meaning: Imports of Raw Materials — chemicals, base metals, industrial intermediates. ~70% of total imports — Indonesia's largest single import category.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks manufacturing-cycle inputs. Surges with manufacturing PMI. Used by analysts as a high-frequency manufacturing-output proxy.

rics.description: Indonesia, TRADE BALANCE (BLN OF $) (INITIAL), Current Prices, Imports & Exports, Monthly, Statistics Indonesia
rics.meaning: Trade Balance (Initial release) — Reuters poll-anchored 'actual' trade balance. Used in surprise-vs-consensus tracking.
rics.how_to_use: Comparison against poll consensus drives IDR same-day at BPS release.

rics.meaning: Trade Balance — total goods trade balance, alternative release. Same as aIDCVISB/A.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

rics.description: Merchandise Exports, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Merchandise Exports, month-over-month change — high-frequency pulse on export momentum.
rics.how_to_use: Highly volatile (±5-10% MoM is normal). Smooth with 3-month average. MoM useful for spotting turning points before YoY confirms.

rics.description: Merchandise Exports, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Merchandise Exports, year-over-year change — pace of export growth. Cleanest signal for trend.
rics.how_to_use: Above 15% YoY = commodity-cycle peak; below -10% = downturn. Indonesia's export YoY swings 30+ pp through commodity cycles. Compare to non-commodity export growth (BPS publishes the breakdown) for underlying-demand vs price-driven growth.

rics.meaning: Merchandise Exports — total monthly goods exports published by BPS-Statistics Indonesia. Released ~3 weeks after month-end, alongside imports and trade balance.
rics.how_to_use: Most-watched Indonesia trade print. ~$22-25B/month recently. Decompose: oil/gas (~10%) vs non-oil/gas (~90%). Within non-oil/gas: coal, palm oil, nickel, manufactures. Surprise vs consensus (~$1B move) drives IDR. Use 3-month moving average for trend.

rics.description: Merchandise Imports, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Merchandise Imports, month-over-month change — high-frequency import-demand pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Volatile. Smooth with 3-month MA for trend. Spike during Lebaran-Eid period (Q2 typically) for consumption-related imports.

rics.description: Merchandise Imports, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Merchandise Imports, year-over-year change — pace of import growth.
rics.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical: surges with domestic demand and capital investment. Falls during IDR weakness episodes (cost-pass-through dampens demand). When import growth exceeds export growth for >2 quarters, current account deficit widens — IDR bearish.

rics.meaning: Merchandise Imports — total monthly goods imports from BPS. Largest categories: capital goods (~25%, machinery + transport eq), raw materials (~70%, chemicals + base metals + intermediates), consumer goods (~5%).
rics.how_to_use: Capital-goods imports lead investment by 2-3 quarters. Sustained surge in capital goods = upcoming GFCF acceleration. Raw materials track manufacturing PMI. Watch oil/gas imports — Indonesia is a net oil importer despite being a gas exporter.

rics.meaning: Visible Trade Balance — monthly goods trade balance from BPS. Same conceptual measure as aIDCBOPA (BoP basis) at higher frequency. Computed as exports minus imports.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia has run a goods-trade surplus consistently since 2020 (~$30-40B annually) on commodity exports. Monthly surplus of $2-3B is normal; >$5B signals commodity-cycle peak. Surprises drive IDR same-day.

rics.description: Visible Trade Balance, month on month, Standardized, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Visible Trade Balance, MoM absolute change — month-over-month change in goods trade balance.
rics.how_to_use: Useful for tracking trade-balance momentum. Sharp swings (>$2B) reflect commodity-price shifts.

rics.description: Visible Trade Balance, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Visible Trade Balance, year-over-year change — change in trade-balance level vs same month a year ago.
rics.how_to_use: Useful for tracking the pace of trade-balance expansion or compression. Sharp YoY decline (e.g., -$3B) signals deteriorating external surplus — IDR bearish.
